timeline.title: Constituent Assembly: Chronological Milestones
timeline.description: Key events in the formation and functioning of the Constituent Assembly of India.

cards.details: The British Cabinet Mission proposed a plan for the transfer of power to Indians. It recommended the formation of a Constituent Assembly with 389 members to frame the Constitution of India.

Elections were held for the Constituent Assembly. The Indian National Congress won 211 seats and the Muslim League won 73 seats. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on December 9, 1946.
The Constituent Assembly met for the first time under the chairmanship of Dr. Sachidanand Sinha (interim). Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the Permanent Chairman.
The Drafting Committee was formed with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as its Chairman. It consisted of 7 members and was tasked with preparing the draft Constitution of India.
The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949. It came into effect on January 26, 1950. India became a Sovereign Democratic Republic on this date.

items.question: Who is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution?
items.answer: **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution. He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.

items.question: Who was the Permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly?
items.answer: **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was the Permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly. He later became the first President of India (1950-1962).

items.question: When did the Constituent Assembly first meet?
items.answer: The Constituent Assembly first met on December 9, 1946. This date is celebrated as Constitution Day since 2015.

items.question: How many members were there in the Constituent Assembly?
items.answer: Total strength: **389** members (296 from British India, 93 from Princely States, and 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces).

items.question: When was the Constitution of India adopted?
items.answer: The Constitution of India was adopted on November 26, 1949. It came into effect on January 26, 1950.

items.question: What was the Cabinet Mission Plan?
items.answer: The **Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946** proposed by the British government for transferring power to Indians and forming a Constituent Assembly to frame the Constitution.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Trap 1: Confusing the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly with the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Dr. Rajendra Prasad = Chairman of Constituent Assembly. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar = Chairman of Drafting Committee.
Trap 2: Thinking that November 26 and January 26 are the same dates. November 26 = Constitution Adopted (1949). January 26 = Constitution came into force (1950, Republic Day).
Trap 3: Believing the Constituent Assembly was entirely elected. Some members from Princely States were nominated by the rulers.
Trap 4: Assuming the Muslim League supported the Constituent Assembly. The Muslim League initially boycotted it and withdrew from it in 1947.
Trap 5: Forgetting that Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is called the Father of the Indian Constitution and not Mahatma Gandhi or Jawaharlal Nehru.
Trap 6: Thinking 1946 was a direct election. Members were elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies (indirect election).
Trap 7: Assuming the Constituent Assembly was formed in 1947. It was formed in 1946 in response to the Cabinet Mission Plan.
Trap 8: Believing the Constituent Assembly took a very short time. It took almost 3 years (Dec 1946 - Nov 1949) with 11 sessions over 165 days.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Explore the history, composition, committees, and contributions of the Constituent Assembly of India.

sections.title: 1. Formation of the Constituent Assembly
sections.content:
The Constituent Assembly of India was formed in 1946 as a result of the Cabinet Mission Plan proposed by the British government under Clement Attlee. The plan aimed to transfer power to Indians and provide a framework for drafting a new Constitution.

Composition
  • Total strength: 389 members
  • 296 from British India (elected by Provincial Assemblies)
  • 93 from Princely States (nominated by rulers)
  • 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces
First Meeting

The Constituent Assembly first met on December 9, 1946. Dr. Sachidanand Sinha was the interim Chairman. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the Permanent Chairman.

Objective Resolution

Presented by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946. It outlined the basic principles for the Constitution. Later became the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

sections.title: 2. Major Committees
sections.content:
The Constituent Assembly formed 13 committees in total to examine various aspects of the Constitution. The most important committees were:

Drafting Committee
  • Formed: August 29, 1947
  • Chairman: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
  • Members: 7 (including N. Mookerjee, T. T. Krishnamachari, etc.)
  • Task: Prepared the draft Constitution
Union Powers Committee
  • Chairman: Jawaharlal Nehru
  • Dealt with Centre-State relations
  • Recommended federal structure with strong Centre
Provincial Constitution Committee
  • Chairman: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
  • Framed provisions for provincial governance
  • Recommended linguistic provinces
Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights
  • Chairman: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
  • Dealt with Fundamental Rights
  • Protected Minorities through specific provisions
Steering Committee
  • Chairman: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
  • Managed day-to-day affairs of the Assembly
  • Decided the order of discussion

sections.title: 3. Key Features of the Indian Constitution
sections.content:
The Indian Constitution adopted on November 26, 1949, is one of the longest written constitutions in the world. It has several distinctive features:

Length & Structure
  • Original text: 395 Articles, 8 Schedules, 22 Parts
  • Current: 448 Articles, 27 Parts, 12 Schedules
  • Longest written constitution in the world
Federal System with Unitary Bias
  • Federal features: Division of powers, bicameral legislature
  • Unitary features: Single citizenship, All India Services, Emergency provisions
  • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it 'Quasi-Federal'
Fundamental Rights
  • Six Fundamental Rights (Articles 14-32)
  • Justiciable (enforced by courts)
  • Can be suspended during Emergency
Directive Principles of State Policy
  • Part IV (Articles 36-51)
  • Non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts)
  • Gguidelines for governance by the State
Secular & Democratic
  • Secular: No state religion
  • Sovereign: India is not under external control
  • Democratic: Government of the people, by the people, for the people
  • Republic: Head of State elected (not hereditary)
